origin.basis: Bontrager is Trek Bicycle Corporation's component brand (Trek US store footer).

manufacturing.basis: The Trek product page does not state where the tire is made.

availability.note: Sold by Trek's US web store; Trek stores and dealers in other regions were not checked for this tire.

name: Aeolus RSL TLR
positioning: Bontrager's 320 TPI cotton-casing tubeless-ready race tire with a race dual compound.
hookless_note: Trek says it is compatible with hooked and hookless rims and that maximum pressures vary by size and rim type.
caveats: The lab sample weighed 314 g against the 285 g claim.
Check the rim maker for hookless pressure limits.

price_observations.conditions: Official store price on 2026-11-01; one tire; shipping and tax at checkout.

image.shown: Tan-wall Aeolus RSL TLR as shown in Trek's primary product photo; a black version is also sold.
image.alt: Bontrager Aeolus RSL TLR road tire with tan sidewalls, standing upright

rights.usage_note: The maker's own product photo, shown from the maker's website; no copy is stored or redistributed by this project, and no license is asserted.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded on 2026-11-04 from a fixed source set: the written reviews on the Sigma Sports and bike-components product pages, read in full through each page's own review list (the newest 15 per page when more exist), every reader comment on Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test pages for this tire, and owner comments in coded Xiaohongshu threads. Counted only owners who describe their own riding; star-only ratings, reviews without riding detail, mounting-only impressions and repeats were left out. Comments on one construction's test page count for that construction unless the owner names the other.

reports.summary: Rolls really smoothly and seems quicker than a Continental, but a flint fragment cut the casing; the owner will return to Continental after another puncture.
The 32 mm feels very smooth and lively just under 60 psi; liked enough on a hire bike to buy.
Very happy after a few rides: close to the P ZERO Race SpeedCORE in ride quality, comfortable and fast.
Liked for five months, until the rear tread delaminated down to the casing in two places at about 1,600-1,700 miles.
No issues in about 100 miles, with rolling that reminds the owner of the GP5000 S TR but without losing pressure.

checks.note: Bontrager tires are not sold there
